hook: Yann LeCun helped build the technique that underlies most of today's computer vision systems. He earned a PhD in computer science from Universite Pierre et Marie Curie in Paris in 1987, working on early ideas that fed into backpropagation based neural network training. At AT&T Bell Labs starting in 1988, he developed convolutional neural networks and built LeNet, a system for reading handwritten digits that was later deployed commercially to process a large share of checks handled by US banks. He went on to become a professor at New York University's Courant Institute, founding the NYU Center for Data Science, and in 2013 joined Facebook, later Meta, as founding director and then Chief AI Scientist of its AI research division. In 2018 he shared the ACM A.M. Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio for their work on deep learning. He left Meta in November 2025 after roughly twelve years to launch Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs, a venture focused on building AI systems around world models rather than only predicting text.
name: Yann LeCun

timeline.impact: Builds early research on neural network training methods that inform his later work
Begins developing convolutional neural networks and the LeNet architecture for image and document recognition

timeline.impact: Documents the convolutional network techniques behind LeNet, deployed to read a significant share of checks processed by US banks

timeline.event: Joins New York University as a professor at the Courant Institute
timeline.impact: Moves into academia while continuing deep learning research

timeline.impact: Builds an academic home for data science research and teaching at NYU

timeline.event: Joins Facebook as founding director of its AI research division
timeline.impact: Leads what becomes Meta's central AI research lab for over a decade

timeline.event: Shares the ACM A.M. Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio
timeline.impact: Receives computing's highest honor for his role in making deep learning practical and influential

quick_facts: Developed convolutional neural networks and LeNet while at AT&T Bell Labs, a system used to read a large share of handwritten checks in the United States
Founded the NYU Center for Data Science in 2012 while a professor at NYU's Courant Institute
Served as founding director and later Chief AI Scientist of Meta's AI research division from 2013 to 2025
Shared the 2018 ACM A.M. Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio
Left Meta in November 2025 to launch Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs, focused on world models
Received the Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering in 2025

achievements.title: Convolutional neural networks and LeNet
achievements.impact: Created the architecture that underlies most modern computer vision systems and built an early commercial application that read handwritten checks.

achievements.title: NYU Center for Data Science
achievements.impact: Founded a research and teaching center in 2012 that helped establish data science as an academic discipline at New York University.

achievements.title: Chief AI Scientist, Meta
achievements.impact: Led Meta's AI research division for roughly twelve years, overseeing fundamental research including work on self-supervised learning.

achievements.title: 2018 ACM A.M. Turing Award
achievements.impact: Recognized, alongside Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio, for conceptual and engineering breakthroughs that made deep neural networks a critical component of computing.

achievements.title: A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence
achievements.impact: Set out a widely discussed research agenda for building AI systems around predictive world models rather than only large language models.
